purpose: choose method for model container recovery (mesh phase)

arguments.decision: Which method should drive recovery of the .PS2 model container layout toward vertex and index data?
arguments.evidence:
User decision: extend the effort to mesh, VU and render reconstruction. Constraints: offline/static only (no debugger windows), claims bounded and falsifiable, milestone and prior verifiers unchanged.
Measured today from the executable's own code (saved Ghidra export): FUN_0011ed90 (6196 bytes, 1549 instructions) is the .ps2 model loader: sprintf '%s.ps2', load via the verified dispatch 00107ce0, then parse the buffer as a chain of sections. FUN_00123908 relocates the name tree: word0 is the byte offset of the next section, rounded up to 16 ((base+word0+15)&~15) on return; it walks 10 count-prefixed arrays adding the base to each entry. This independently matches my verified invariants (first u32 equals name-pool end offset in 56/56; zero pad to 16; 9 groups in every model). FUN_0022ba30 (1548 bytes) parses the next section: three counts then (n1+n2+n3) 12-byte entries and allocates 0x400 bytes per entry for the first count. Back in FUN_0011ed90: a count s6 then s6 records of 0x34 bytes, then more loops. Raw bytes alone (debug.ps2, 49COUPE.PS2) look like sparse memory-image structs with small counters and index runs, so blind layout guessing from bytes is slow.
Jev finds over loader chunks: pointer-relocation 'partial' 0.67, name-tree-walk 'absent' 0.21 (not in this function), float-field handling 'answered' 0.90.
No hardware or emulator oracle is available; an executable-derived parser is checkable by consuming every one of the 56 real model files exactly to EOF.
arguments.priorities: Falsifiable results on all 56 real files; evidence from the game's own code rather than guesses; no windows or emulator focus; incremental deliverables with tests; bounded claims; keep unresolved items listed.

candidates.description: Read each section parser in the executable (name-tree relocator, section 2 parser, the 0x34-stride record loop and later loops), translate it into a Python section walker one section at a time, and require the chain to land exactly on end-of-file for all 56 models, with negative tests on malformed section counts.
Run FUN_0011ed90 under a headless Ghidra pcode emulator with stubs for allocators and I/O against real files and record memory reads and writes.
Infer the vertex and index layout from byte statistics and visual plots of the model files without using the executable.
Start from the VU1 microprogram in .vutext and infer the vertex format from how it consumes data.

requirements: Each step yields a check that can fail on real files (for example, a section chain that must end exactly at end-of-file).
The method needs no GUI, emulator window or focus change.
